amish.church_discipline:
Among the Amish, a baptized member who willfully breaks the church's agreed Ordnung and will not repent is placed under the Bann. The ordinary name for the everyday working of that discipline is shunning, or Meidung: the congregation withdraws from ordinary table fellowship, business partnership, and easy social traffic with the person. The aim, as members describe it, is not revenge but to make the break visible, to guard the church from the same offense, and to move the straying member to come back in humility and be restored.

How far Meidung reaches is not the same in every affiliation. Some districts limit avoidance mainly to communion and shared meals. Stricter Old Order groups extend it into the household, so that a banned spouse or child eats apart. Only the local Gmee, with the bishop, may put a member under the Bann or take the Bann off after a public confession. Unbaptized children are not shunned; the Bann belongs to those who have already made their own vow to the church.
